channel.title: Europe AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of European political, economic and security developments

item.title: 'Anger in the streets': Tens of thousands protest in Spain over housing crisis
item.description: More than 50 protests took place on Saturday after the government failed to get emergency legislation through parliament.

item.title: Russia hits second major bridge in Ukraine's capital Kyiv
item.description: The strike on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge comes after repeat attacks on another major bridge in Ukraine's capital.

item.title: School protests send shivers down French government's spine
item.description: A movement that started nearly two weeks ago has spread, and in France young people on the streets spells trouble, writes Hugh Schofield.

item.title: Putin warns West that Russia is ready to use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad
item.description: The Russian leader insists Moscow is "not threatening anyone" and is merely responding to statements by Western leaders.

item.title: Seoul warns 'further action' if Ukraine does not apologise over prisoner-of-war row
item.description: President Lee Jae Myung also accused Kyiv of "attempting to provoke a war on the Korean Peninsula".

item.title: Spanish PM Sánchez loses key housing crisis vote after eviction of woman, 87
item.description: The defeat raises pressure on Sánchez to call a snap election, after a series of scandals affecting his party and allies.

item.title: Russian dissident Garry Kasparov says US warned him of danger to his life
item.description: "My family and I will not truly be safe as long as Putin is in power," says the former chess world champion.

item.title: Six smugglers jailed for manslaughter over worst Channel small boats disaster
item.description: Thirty-one migrants died when their boat went down in November 2021. The trial found that the guilty men were part of two smuggling networks.

item.title: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign
item.description: Ukraine's remaining steelworks, a vital part of its economy, have all but ground to a halt because of relentless attacks.

item.title: Rosenberg: Putin shows no sign of stopping the war as Russia doubles down on Ukraine
item.description: A foreign policy speech by the Russian president will be keenly watched, but all signs point to the full-scale invasion continuing.

item.title: Migrants using longer, more dangerous routes across Channel
item.description: The government says it is bearing down on dangerous small boat crossings.

item.title: As Merz scrambles for support, Germany's identity crisis is laid bare
item.description: Voters are turning away from the centre in Germany as fears grow about the economy and migration.

item.title: Will Spain's housing crisis lead to a snap election?
item.description: The BBC's Guy Hedgecoe is in Madrid, where a series of marches have been scheduled, after Spain's Congress rejected measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis.

item.title: Why are students protesting at schools in France?
item.description: The BBC's Hugh Schofield is in Paris as a wave of school protests over overcrowded classes and teacher shortages spreads across France.

item.title: Fires and blockades as students stage school protests across France
item.description: More than 400 people, mainly minors, were arrested on Tuesday, the country's interior minister says.

item.title: People escape historic Kyiv building hit by Russian drone
item.description: The BBC's Paul Adams reports from the scene of the strike on Ukraine's National Academy of Sciences.

item.title: Latvian PM’s election win boosts chances for pro-Ukraine coalition
item.description: Andris Kulbergs’ party finished more than 20 percentage points ahead of far-right Latvia First.

item.title: Security-Update: Krieg bei Social Media – mit Marcel Bohnert
item.description: Mehr als die Hälfte der jungen Wähler entscheidet sich bei jüngsten Landtagswahlen für Parteien, die der Ukraine-Unterstützung kritisch gegenüberstehen. Der Grund dafür liegt nicht nur in klassischen Debatten, sondern auf Plattformen wie TikTok, Instagram und X. Dort tobt längst ein massiver Informationskrieg, in dem ausländische Akteure und Algorithmen um die Deutungshoheit kämpfen. Marcel Bohnert, Oberstleutnant […]

item.title: Germany’s Merz visits Kyiv amid fears of ‘hardest’ winter in war
item.description: The visit has been overshadowed by heavy Russian attacks on Kyiv as well as tensions over Ukraine's EU membership prospects

item.title: EU neighbors shun Kyiv’s plea to free trapped grain
item.description: Poland and Romania said there’s nothing more they can do to help Ukraine export its grain through Europe, as the blockade in the Black Sea continues.
